purpose: Paper-derived hypotheses that are ready to become code. An item enters when a note names the metric, the baseline, and the failure it addresses. It leaves when eval/ settles it.

experiments.title: Calibration acceptance uses p95 and temporal jitter, not RMS alone
experiments.hypothesis: A calibration that passes an RMS gate can still inject >1 ft p95 error and visible speed noise; adding p95 and a static-point jitter test changes which calibrations we accept.
experiments.metric: p95 reprojection error (ft), static-point jitter (ft, 100 frames)
experiments.baseline: RMS only; current 0.696 ft RMS on the Luka/Ayton clip
experiments.expected_effect: Reject 1-2 calibrations that currently pass; no change to downstream F1 until events are re-scored

experiments.title: Compare 4-point, 8-point, and keypoint-model calibration on fixed gym footage
experiments.hypothesis: For a static gym camera, 6-8 well-spread points materially reduce p95 error versus 4, but the learned keypoint model still fails on non-NBA courts.
experiments.metric: median/RMS/p95 reprojection ft; downstream speed error
experiments.expected_effect: p95 improves without new data; keypoint model remains unusable on gym

experiments.title: Measure real ball recall against labeled positions
experiments.hypothesis: The 35.1% frame-coverage number is not recall; on labeled frames, recall@15px will be higher for visible balls and near zero under occlusion, changing where we invest.
experiments.metric: recall@5px, recall@15px, precision at conf=0.25
experiments.expected_effect: A defensible recall number and a visibility-bucket breakdown

experiments.title: Low-score association for the ball
experiments.hypothesis: ByteTrack's second association stage recovers ball frames that the 0.25 threshold discards, improving shot F1 without increasing false events.
experiments.metric: shot F1 @5 frames; false-positive events; ball track fragments
experiments.expected_effect: Recall up; precision must not drop beyond the noise floor

experiments.title: Gravity-constrained interpolation
experiments.hypothesis: A constant-acceleration model with a gravity prior rejects physically impossible interpolations better than a max-speed gate, reducing fake shot trajectories.
experiments.metric: shot F1; impossible-trajectory rate; interpolated-frame count
experiments.expected_effect: Fewer false shots during passes and deflections

experiments.title: Add HOTA to the tracking scorecard
experiments.hypothesis: MOTA/IDF1 hide association failures that HOTA exposes; adding HOTA changes the tracker recommendation on at least one clip.
experiments.metric: HOTA, DetA, AssA
experiments.expected_effect: A diagnostic split between detection and association errors

experiments.title: Camera-motion compensation for broadcast tracking
experiments.hypothesis: BoT-SORT-style GMC reduces ID switches on pan/zoom clips without hurting static clips.
experiments.metric: HOTA, ID switches, fragments
experiments.expected_effect: Fewer switches on pans; neutral on static

experiments.title: Freeze the event ontology v1
experiments.hypothesis: A single JSON ontology with IDs and definitions reduces label disagreement and makes detectors comparable; the current six classes miss rebounds, fouls, and violations.
experiments.metric: ontology coverage of BasketEvent classes; label agreement (kappa)
experiments.baseline: Six ClipResult event lists, no shared IDs
experiments.expected_effect: A machine-readable contract and a gap list

experiments.title: Rule-based rebound detection
experiments.hypothesis: A rebound can be detected from shot outcome + ball descent + first player to control, with usable precision on labeled clips.
experiments.metric: rebound P/R/F1 @15 frames; offensive/defensive split
experiments.expected_effect: First outcome event class; exposes ball-tracking gaps at the rim

experiments.title: DINOv2 vs HSV K-means for team assignment
experiments.hypothesis: Frozen DINOv2 features improve team assignment when jersey colors are similar, but not when they are already distinct.
experiments.metric: team accuracy per game; confusion matrix; abstention rate
experiments.expected_effect: Gain concentrated in the similar-jersey clips

experiments.title: Player retrieval benchmark from frozen features
experiments.hypothesis: DINOv2 embeddings support same-player retrieval across frames well enough to seed ReID, even without basketball-specific fine-tuning.
experiments.metric: mAP@10 on same/different player pairs
experiments.expected_effect: A go/no-go for a ReID embedding head

experiments.title: Make the court template a ruleset parameter
experiments.hypothesis: Hard-coded NBA dimensions misclassify FIBA/NCAA shots; a ruleset config removes a silent error class.
experiments.metric: shot-type accuracy by ruleset; 3-point classification errors
experiments.expected_effect: Correct shot type on non-NBA footage

experiments.title: Generate Pydantic enums from the ontology
experiments.hypothesis: Generating event enums from one JSON file prevents code/label drift and fails tests on unknown IDs.
experiments.metric: unknown-ID test failures; schema coverage
experiments.expected_effect: Contract enforcement; no behavior change

experiments.title: Possession-level matchup assignment
experiments.hypothesis: Hungarian assignment plus temporal smoothing yields stable offensive-defensive matchups, the prerequisite for coverage classification.
experiments.metric: assignment stability; coach agreement on 20 possessions
experiments.expected_effect: Fewer spurious switches; usable matchup data

experiments.title: Zone-average xPTS baseline
experiments.hypothesis: A zone-average points-per-shot baseline is already more useful to a coach than raw FG%, and is the bar any model must beat.
experiments.metric: log loss, Brier, calibration curve
experiments.expected_effect: Zone baseline implemented: Denver 2023-24 Brier 0.2354, log loss 0.6636 on 16 held-out games; xPTS ordering RA 1.303 > corner 3 1.153 > above-break 3 1.127 > paint 0.975 > mid-range 0.910.

experiments.title: Reconcile possession accounting with the box score
experiments.hypothesis: Our POSS/ORtg/DRtg can be made to match the public box score on one game, exposing every edge case in the ledger.
experiments.metric: absolute difference in POSS, ORtg, DRtg, Four Factors
experiments.expected_effect: A trustworthy accounting layer before any tracking metric

experiments.title: Paired bootstrap baseline vs candidate
experiments.hypothesis: A paired bootstrap over clips answers the ship/no-ship question more tightly than comparing two independent intervals.
experiments.metric: paired difference CI; minimum detectable effect
experiments.expected_effect: Better decisions on small clip counts

experiments.title: Add footage_type and calibration metadata to ClipResult
experiments.hypothesis: Without a regime field, scorecards average a broadcast win over a gym collapse; adding metadata makes the breakdown possible.
experiments.metric: scorecard completeness; per-regime F1
experiments.expected_effect: A regime-aware scorecard

experiments.title: Measure the broadcast-to-gym detection gap
experiments.hypothesis: The current detector loses substantial recall on fixed-gym footage, and per-regime thresholds recover part of it.
experiments.metric: mAP@50 and recall by regime; threshold sweep
experiments.expected_effect: A quantified domain gap and a per-regime operating point

experiments.title: Screen/PnR proposal-stage result
experiments.hypothesis: The learned single-frame screen/PnR detector is useful as a high-recall candidate generator but not as a final event detector; the evidence supports proposal-only, not integration.
experiments.metric: screen/PnR event P/R/F1 at +/-15 frames; candidate recall; candidates per clip
experiments.baseline: rule-based screen detector on the same 60 clips
experiments.expected_effect: Proposal-only: screen F1 0.244 at 0.25 (0.458 at 0.50); PnR 0.209 at 0.25 (0.364 at 0.50); no statistically measured win over the rule

experiments.title: Pair/temporal screen classifier
experiments.hypothesis: A second-stage pair/temporal classifier over candidate clips can lift precision at recall >= 0.6 by using screener, cutter, and defender tracks plus interval context.
experiments.metric: event-level P/R/F1; pair-assignment accuracy; interval IoU
experiments.baseline: proposal-stage YOLO at a recall-oriented threshold
experiments.expected_effect: Precision lift at fixed recall; requires upstream tracking/team/possession scorecard and pair labels

experiments.title: Logistic xPTS with distance, angle, and contest
experiments.hypothesis: A logistic model with distance, angle, shot type, and contest beats the zone baseline on grouped log loss and calibration, especially for player-level shots.
experiments.metric: grouped log loss, Brier, calibration curve
experiments.baseline: zone baseline: Denver Brier 0.2354, log loss 0.6636
experiments.expected_effect: Neutral vs zone baseline: Denver Brier 0.2345 vs 0.2354, log loss 0.6613 vs 0.6636; Curry 0.2351 vs 0.2362, 0.6630 vs 0.6653. Within noise; middle bins remain overconfident.

experiments.title: Contest-aware xPTS
experiments.hypothesis: Adding defender distance and closeout speed at release will improve xPTS calibration beyond a location-only zone/logistic baseline, especially in the middle probability bins.
experiments.metric: grouped log loss, Brier, calibration curve
experiments.expected_effect: Better calibration in the 0.35-0.55 bins; requires defender tracking at release
experiments.eval_gate: requires reliable defender distance at release

experiments.title: Freeze play taxonomy v1
experiments.hypothesis: A small, orthogonal taxonomy of play types, coverages, and families makes play recognition comparable and exposes ontology gaps.
experiments.metric: taxonomy coverage; label agreement (kappa)
experiments.expected_effect: Machine-readable taxonomy v1: 11 play types, 10 coverages, 7 families

experiments.title: Play-recognition baseline on 50 possessions
experiments.hypothesis: A rules-based screen/coverage detector and a sequence model on tracking features can beat a naive PnR-vs-ISO baseline at the possession level.
experiments.metric: per-possession top-1/top-3 accuracy; per-class confusion; calibration
experiments.expected_effect: A defensible play-type baseline and a list of confusable pairs

experiments.title: Counter mapping from coverage to action
experiments.hypothesis: A coach-reviewed table mapping coverage (drop, switch, ice, zone, press) to a counter action is more useful than a single play-type label.
experiments.metric: coach agreement; counter usability
experiments.expected_effect: A ranked counter card with preconditions and evidence

experiments.title: NBA box-score Four Factors baseline
experiments.hypothesis: The possession ledger and Four Factors can be computed from an NBA box score and match hand calculations before applying them to video.
experiments.metric: POSS, ORtg, DRtg, Four Factors vs hand calculation
experiments.expected_effect: Validated accounting layer; IND 121-CLE 116: POSS 107.6/103.0, ORtg 112.5/112.6, pace 105.3

experiments.title: NBA game report v0
experiments.hypothesis: A one-page report combining Four Factors and shot profile is more useful to a coach than either table alone, and it exposes which perception layers are missing.
experiments.metric: report completeness; coach usability
experiments.baseline: separate Four Factors and shot tables
experiments.expected_effect: One-page Markdown report; v0 has no tracking, contest, or play recognition

experiments.title: Calibrate the three Phase B games
experiments.hypothesis: A fixed/panning Hudl-like camera can be calibrated to <1 ft p95 on a usable segment, enabling the shot chart.
experiments.metric: median/RMS/p95 reprojection ft; temporal jitter
experiments.expected_effect: 3 games calibrated; p95 < 1 ft on usable segments

experiments.title: NBA Stats API PBP cross-check
experiments.hypothesis: The official NBA Stats API v3 is an independent second source that can validate the canonical ESPN-based state layer's points and possession count.
experiments.metric: points exactness; possession count vs box estimate
experiments.expected_effect: 205 possessions vs 210.6 estimate; points 121/116 exact; 2.7% POSS gap

experiments.title: Cross-source possession ledger comparison
experiments.hypothesis: Comparing the NBA Stats and ESPN ledgers on the same game exposes possession-boundary disagreements that neither source reveals alone.
experiments.metric: points per team; possession count; boundary disagreement count
experiments.expected_effect: A concrete list of boundary disagreements to debug
experiments.eval_gate: one game mapped across NBA game id and ESPN event id

experiments.title: Per-quarter possession ledger reconciliation
experiments.hypothesis: Per-quarter reconciliation exposes and-1, technical, and team-rebound edge cases and improves the ledger.
experiments.metric: per-quarter points and possession counts
experiments.expected_effect: edge-case inventory and a tighter POSS match

experiments.title: NBA Synergy team play-type profile
experiments.hypothesis: The NBA Synergy play-type endpoint gives a usable aggregate answer to what a team runs and how efficient it is, and a prior for video play recognition.
experiments.metric: play-type frequency, PPP, eFG%, TOV%, FT%, percentile
experiments.expected_effect: 30 teams x 11 play types cached; IND 2023-24 profile documented

experiments.title: Player-level play-type profiles
experiments.hypothesis: Player-level Synergy profiles identify each player's action mix and efficiency, which is more actionable for matchup planning than a team aggregate.
experiments.metric: player play-type frequency and PPP vs team/league
experiments.expected_effect: Pacers rotation and Haliburton profile documented; player-level PnR/spot-up/transition mix exposed

experiments.title: Video play recognition vs Synergy frequencies
experiments.hypothesis: A per-possession video play classifier can be compared with Synergy's aggregate frequencies on the same team and season, exposing where our labels and model disagree.
experiments.metric: per-possession top-1/top-3; frequency distance vs Synergy
experiments.expected_effect: A label/model gap report; requires per-possession labels

experiments.title: Pre-game scout report v0
experiments.hypothesis: Combining team Four Factors, Synergy play types, player roles, and shot profile into one page gives a usable pre-game prior.
experiments.metric: report completeness; source values match caches
experiments.expected_effect: One-page IND 2023-24 report: 2nd ORtg, 24th DRtg, 2nd pace

experiments.title: Opponent-specific scout report
experiments.hypothesis: Combining both teams profiles into a matchup page surfaces attack/defend priorities better than a single-team page.
experiments.metric: matchup page completeness; coach review
experiments.expected_effect: One matchup page with explicit attack/defend priorities

experiments.title: Scorebug clock alignment for shot events
experiments.hypothesis: The broadcast scorebug clock can align PBP shot events to live-play frames more reliably than sparse manual anchors.
experiments.metric: aligned events / selected; clock difference
experiments.expected_effect: 18/20 aligned; offsets up to 13s corrected

experiments.title: Shot attempt detector baseline
experiments.hypothesis: The existing ball-trajectory shot detector finds at least one shot in PBP-centered NBA broadcast clips.
experiments.metric: clip-level detection; by shot type
experiments.expected_effect: 10/20 clips detected; layups/mid-range weak

experiments.title: Layup and rim attempt detector
experiments.hypothesis: Ball-near-rim plus trajectory features recover layup and dunk attempts that the vertical-streak detector misses.
experiments.metric: recall/precision on layup/dunk clips
experiments.expected_effect: Recover at least 8/10 at-rim attempts

experiments.title: Rebound detector
experiments.hypothesis: Ball-off-rim plus player proximity and possession change detects offensive and defensive rebounds on missed shots.
experiments.metric: rebound F1; offensive/defensive split
experiments.expected_effect: First video rebound baseline

experiments.title: Made/miss classifier
experiments.hypothesis: Rim, net, and ball-trajectory features separate made from missed shots on scorebug-aligned clips.
experiments.metric: accuracy/AUC on made vs missed
experiments.expected_effect: A measurable made/miss baseline

experiments.title: Clean negative set for shot attempts
experiments.hypothesis: Scorebug-aligned turnover possessions with no shot attempt give a trustworthy false-positive rate for shot detectors.
experiments.metric: clip-level false-positive rate
experiments.expected_effect: 10 clean turnover negatives; baseline 1/10 FP, rise80 3/10, rise60 6/10

experiments.title: Pose and geometry shot-candidate filter
experiments.hypothesis: Wrist-above-elbow and ball-player-rim geometry reject drives and passes admitted by a high-recall shot candidate threshold.
experiments.metric: precision/recall on 20 positives + 10 clean negatives
experiments.expected_effect: Keep >=20/20 recall and cut clean-negative FPs below 3/10
